items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I also met a pianist and accordionist called Teddy Weatherford... Teddy Weatherford had never been in Europe and had decided that he was coming back with us.

ctx.x: I had a very large room assigned to me in the hotel until other lodgings could be arranged. The bed was very large also and had cheesecloth curtains on the four sides which was to keep the mosquitos from having a good time when you went to sleep at night. Mr. Farletti presented us to the assistant manager who was an Indian named D.R. Banerjee who was to look after us personally.

On the left side of the Taj facing the bay was a monument called the Gateway to India and to the left of that was a smaller hotel owned by the Taj direction called the Mayfair. I also met a pianist and accordionist called Teddy Weatherford. Teddy was an American Negro who had travelled over most of the Far East and had a big name amongst the early jazz musicians before I came on the scene. Teddy had been in India quite a few years and was very popular with the English dignitaries and others in the Bombay High…

The next day we started rehearsing the show which included six acts with a troupe of English girls and a tap dancer named Rosalind Wade. A French trombonist who had been in Bombay for sometime was added to the orchestra which made ten musicians in the orchestra. We opened a couple of days later and everything went fine. Arthur Lanier sang ballads and we formed a quartet with Leon, Ollie Tines, Lanier and myself to sing variety numbers. The job was not hard because we worked 4 nights and 2 matinees a week.
